summary: William Reeve worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society (~1815–1824 and ~1827–1834) and as minister at Oswestry Congregational Church (1836–1843).

William Robertson was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He served as Principal of the University of Edinburgh (1762–1792) and was a member of the Royal Society of Edinburgh and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

William Ross Hardie studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1876–1880) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1880–1884). He held posts at the University of Oxford (~1884–1895) and the University of Edinburgh (~1895–1916).

William Roxburgh worked in Indology and botany after studying at the University of Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Marischal College. He served with the East India Company and headed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

William S. Waldron worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, Ichijo Ogawa, and Seiki Miyashita, and held posts at Otani University and Middlebury College (attested 2003).

William Sandys Wright Vaux worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Balliol College, Oxford, he served at the British Museum (1841; Keeper of Coins and Medals 1861–1870) and was Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1876–1885).
William Sax is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Canterbury (attested 2000) and became Professor Emeritus at Heidelberg University in 2025.

William Sidney Allen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and Arthur James Beattie. He lectured at SOAS (1948–1951) and was Professor of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1955–1982).
William Spottiswoode, active in Indology, studied at Balliol College, Oxford (1842–1845). In 1846, he held posts at Balliol College and at Eyre & Spottiswoode.

William Stede worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studying at Göttingen, Jena, and Leipzig (Ph.D. 1913). He held posts at the University of Liverpool, SOAS, the University of London, and served as President of the Pali Text Society (1950–1958).
William Taylor worked in Indology. He served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society (1824–1845) and held a post as a cataloguer at Madras College.

William Van Gordon is a researcher in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

William Ward was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Brearley Theological Academy and Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett. He was a missionary at Serampore Mission (~1800–1823) and co-founded Serampore College in 1818.

William Wilfred Webb was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Aberdeen. He served in the Indian Medical Service, the Bengal Army (~1882–1894), and as Secretary at the Army Medical School (1893–1902).

William Wilson Hunter worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887), was Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University (1886–1887), and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1895–1900).

William Woodville Rockhill specialized in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr and Lycée Condorcet, and was taught by Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux.

William Wright was an Arabic linguist educated at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He held professorships at University College London, Trinity College Dublin, and the University of Cambridge (1870–1889), and worked at the British Museum (1861–1870).
William Yates was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bristol Baptist College and Brown University. He also studied under William Carey from ~1815 to 1834.

Willibald Kirfel was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He worked as a librarian at Bonn University Library before serving as Professor of Indology at the University of Bonn from 1922 to 1953.

Willy Bang-Kaup worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin at KU Leuven, taught at KU Leuven, and held professorships at Goethe University Frankfurt (1917) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1918).
